Project Python Foundations: FoodHub Data Analysis¶

Context¶

The number of restaurants in New York is increasing day by day. Lots of students and busy professionals rely on those restaurants due to their hectic lifestyles. Online food delivery service is a great option for them. It provides them with good food from their favorite restaurants. A food aggregator company FoodHub offers access to multiple restaurants through a single smartphone app.

The app allows the restaurants to receive a direct online order from a customer. The app assigns a delivery person from the company to pick up the order after it is confirmed by the restaurant. The delivery person then uses the map to reach the restaurant and waits for the food package. Once the food package is handed over to the delivery person, he/she confirms the pick-up in the app and travels to the customer's location to deliver the food. The delivery person confirms the drop-off in the app after delivering the food package to the customer. The customer can rate the order in the app. The food aggregator earns money by collecting a fixed margin of the delivery order from the restaurants.

Objective¶

The food aggregator company has stored the data of the different orders made by the registered customers in their online portal. They want to analyze the data to get a fair idea about the demand of different restaurants which will help them in enhancing their customer experience. Suppose you are hired as a Data Scientist in this company and the Data Science team has shared some of the key questions that need to be answered. Perform the data analysis to find answers to these questions that will help the company to improve the business.

Data Description¶

The data contains the different data related to a food order. The detailed data dictionary is given below.

Data Dictionary¶

  • order_id: Unique ID of the order
  • customer_id: ID of the customer who ordered the food
  • restaurant_name: Name of the restaurant
  • cuisine_type: Cuisine ordered by the customer
  • cost_of_the_order: Cost of the order
  • day_of_the_week: Indicates whether the order is placed on a weekday or weekend (The weekday is from Monday to Friday and the weekend is Saturday and Sunday)
  • rating: Rating given by the customer out of 5
  • food_preparation_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the restaurant to prepare the food. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the restaurant's order confirmation and the delivery person's pick-up confirmation.
  • delivery_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the delivery person to deliver the food package. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the delivery person's pick-up confirmation and drop-off information

# So rating column does contain some missing values i-e Not Given, lets create another column that contains the mean of ratings instead of missing values
df['processed_rating'] = df['rating'].replace("Not given", np.nan)
df['processed_rating'] = df['processed_rating'].astype(float)
df['processed_rating'] = df['processed_rating'].fillna(df['processed_rating'].mean())

Univariate Analysis Observations¶

1. cost_of_the_order¶

  • The distribution is slightly right-skewed, with most orders falling between $10 and $20 .
  • A few high-cost orders act as outliers.
  • The frequency drops sharply beyond the $20-25 range.

2. food_preparation_time¶

  • The data is relatively uniformly distributed with no distinct peaks.
  • Preparation times are mostly between 20 and 35 minutes.
  • The distribution suggests consistent kitchen performance.

3. delivery_time¶

  • Most deliveries occur between 20 and 30 minutes.
  • The count gradually decreases as delivery time increases.
  • Slight right skewness is observed.

4. processed_rating¶

  • The ratings are heavily skewed toward higher values.
  • Most common ratings are 4.0 and 5.0.
  • Few ratings fall below 4, indicating a generally positive response.

5. cuisine_type¶

  • American and Japanese cuisines are the most frequently ordered.
  • Other cuisines such as Vietnamese, Spanish, and French have significantly fewer entries.
  • The distribution is highly imbalanced, with a strong preference for specific cuisine types.

6. day_of_the_week¶

  • Order counts are noticeably higher on weekends compared to weekdays.
  • Saturday and Sunday show peak activity, while mid-week days have relatively fewer orders.
  • This suggests consumer behavior is influenced by weekly schedules.

7. rating¶

  • A large portion of ratings are marked as "Not given," indicating missing data.
  • Among the provided ratings, 5-star ratings are the most common, followed by 4-star.
  • Very few ratings are 3 or below, suggesting a positive bias in customer feedback.

Question 13: The company wants to provide a promotional offer in the advertisement of the restaurants. The condition to get the offer is that the restaurants must have a rating count of more than 50 and the average rating should be greater than 4. Find the restaurants fulfilling the criteria to get the promotional offer. [3 marks]¶

In [113]:
# Write the code here
filtered_df = df[df['rating'] != 'Not given'].copy()
filtered_df['rating'] = filtered_df['rating'].astype(float)
restaurant_rating_summary = filtered_df.groupby('restaurant_name')['rating'].agg(['count', 'mean'])
qualified_restaurants = restaurant_rating_summary[
    (restaurant_rating_summary['count'] >= 50) &
    (restaurant_rating_summary['mean'] > 4)
]

print(qualified_restaurants)

                           count      mean
restaurant_name                           
Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken     64  4.328125
Blue Ribbon Sushi             73  4.219178
Shake Shack                  133  4.278195
The Meatball Shop             84  4.511905

Observations:¶

  • Only a subset of restaurants met both criteria: receiving more than 50 ratings and maintaining an average rating above 4.0.
  • These qualifying restaurants reflect high customer engagement (frequent feedback) and strong performance in service quality.
  • Most restaurants failed to meet the threshold due to either a low number of ratings or a moderate average rating.
  • The selected restaurants are ideal candidates for promotional advertisements, as they demonstrate both popularity and customer satisfaction.
  • This data-driven selection ensures that marketing efforts are targeted toward top-performing restaurants, likely improving campaign success.

Question 14: The company charges the restaurant 25% on the orders having cost greater than 20 dollars and 15% on the orders having cost greater than 5 dollars. Find the net revenue generated by the company across all orders. [3 marks]¶

In [114]:
# Write the code here
def calculate_revenue(row):
    cost = row['cost_of_the_order']
    if cost > 20:
        return cost * 0.25
    elif cost > 5:
        return cost * 0.15
    else:
        return 0

df['revenue'] = df.apply(calculate_revenue, axis=1)
net_revenue = df['revenue'].sum()
print(f"Net revenue generated by the company: ${net_revenue:.2f}")

Net revenue generated by the company: $6166.30

Observations:¶

  • The company has a net revenue of $6166.30

Conclusion and Recommendations¶

Question 17: What are your conclusions from the analysis? What recommendations would you like to share to help improve the business? (You can use cuisine type and feedback ratings to drive your business recommendations.) [6 marks]¶

Conclusions:¶

  • Customer Satisfaction: The majority of ratings are 4 and above indicating High Customer Satisfaction
  • Cuisine Preferences: American, Japanese, Italin and Chineese are the most frequently ordered, especially on weekends.-
  • Delivery Performance: A noticeable portion of orders i-e 10.54% take more then 60 minutes to prepare and deliver, also delivery is faster on weekends then weekdays
  • High-Performing Restaurants: Only a few restaurants meet the criteria for high-performance indicating room for improvement across many vedors

Recommendations:¶

  1. Boost Feedback Collection

    • Encourage customers to leave ratings with small incentives.

  2. Promote High-Rated, Low-Order Cuisines

    • Use discounts or app banners to promote quality cuisines with low visibility.

  3. Improve Weekday Delivery Times

    • Optimize delivery routes or shift staffing to reduce delays on weekdays.

  4. Reward Loyal Customers

    • Offer exclusive vouchers or loyalty points to top repeat customers.

  5. Highlight Top Restaurants

    • Feature high-rated restaurants more prominently in the app.

  6. Support Low-Rated Vendors

    • Share performance reports and offer training to improve service.

  7. Upsell to Higher Order Values

    • Recommend add-ons to push orders above $20 for better margins.
